After `import config from "./config"`, `config.load` is a property of the default export. It is not the named export `load` of the module. If the default export has no such property, you get `undefined`. If it has one, a named import says the same thing more directly and lets bundlers drop the exports you do not use.

The rule reads the imported module and reports `config.load` and `const { load } = config` if the module has a named export `load`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* file "config.js" */}
```js config.js
export function load(path) {
  return JSON.parse(read(path));
}

export default { port: 3000 };
```

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
import config from "./config";

config.load("./app.json");
const { load } = config;
```

Not reported:

{/* file "config.js" */}
```js config.js
export function load(path) {
  return JSON.parse(read(path));
}

export default { port: 3000 };
```

{/* good */}
```js
import config, { load } from "./config";

load("./app.json");
listen(config.port);
```
